question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(165,0.6),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X=90).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places. *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,-1.5\,$ $\,0.0668\,$ $\,0.0655\,$ $\,0.0643\,$
$\,-1.4\,$ $\,0.0808\,$ $\,0.0793\,$ $\,0.0778\,$
$\,-1.3\,$ $\,0.0968\,$ $\,0.0951\,$ $\,0.0934\,$
$z$$\,0.05\,$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$
$\,-1.5\,$ $\,0.0606\,$ $\,0.0594\,$ $\,0.0582\,$
$\,-1.4\,$ $\,0.0735\,$ $\,0.0722\,$ $\,0.0708\,$
$\,-1.3\,$ $\,0.0885\,$ $\,0.0869\,$ $\,0.0854\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=165$ and $p=0.6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =165\cdot 0.6 \\  & =99 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =165\cdot (1-0.6) \\  & =66 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(165)(0.6)=99
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(165)(0.6)(1-0.6)=39.6.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(99,39.6).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=90).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=90)≈P(89.5\le Y\le 90.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(89.5\le Y\le 90.5) & =P(\frac{89.5-99}{\sqrt{39.6}}\le Z\le \frac{90.5-99}{\sqrt{39.6}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.51\le Z\le -1.35) \\  & =P(Z\le -1.35)-P(Z<-1.51) \\  & =P(Z\le -1.35)-P(Z\le -1.51) \\  & =Φ(-1.35)-Φ(-1.51) \\  & =0.0885-0.0655 \\  & =0.023\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=90)≈0.023.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0227.$
